 'Threepeat' MEAC champions host Delaware State for Senior & High School Band Day; fans urged to fill stadium with garnet
 ORANGEBURG, S.C. — Fresh off clinching their third consecutive Mid-Eastern Athletic Conference (MEAC) football championship, the South Carolina State Bulldogs are calling on Bulldog Nation to turn out at Oliver C. Dawson Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21, for their regular-season finale against Delaware State.
 Kickoff is scheduled for 1:30 p.m.
 Fans are encouraged to wear garnet and pack the stands in a show of Bulldog pride as SC State celebrates Senior & High School Band Day and its latest conference championship. Game tickets and prepaid parking passes are available at scsuathletics.com .

 SC State reminds fans, students, employees and campus visitors to plan ahead for game day traffic, parking restrictions and security procedures designed to maintain a safe and enjoyable environment.
 The university will implement its established game day safety protocols, including controlled campus access, identification checks, parking enforcement and security screening at stadium entrances.
 Campus access and traffic
 All guests entering campus must have a valid game ticket, whether arriving on foot or in a vehicle. Every occupant of a vehicle must have a ticket. Vehicles entering campus must also have a valid parking pass.
 Current SC State students must present their valid university identification cards for campus and stadium access.
 General parking passholders may enter at Gate 2 (Russell and Pinckney streets) or Gate 1A (Russell and Baldwin streets) until campus lots are full.
 Visitors should expect increased traffic around campus before and after the game. University officials encourage fans to arrive early, follow posted signs and comply with directions from law enforcement officers and parking personnel.
 Campus access will be controlled through designated entry points. Motorists should not attempt to enter through closed or restricted gates. Traffic patterns may be adjusted as needed to accommodate pedestrian safety and vehicle movement.
 Parking restrictions
 All Hugine Suites parking lots will be reserved exclusively for authorized law enforcement and security personnel during the game day security period.
 Students and other motorists must remove their vehicles from Hugine Suites parking lots by noon Friday, Nov. 20. The restriction will remain in effect until noon Sunday, Nov. 22.
 Vehicles remaining in the restricted lots after the Friday deadline will be subject to towing.
 Alternative parking will be available in the Mays I and II area and the new gravel lot behind Crawford-Zimmerman.
 Fans should park only in authorized areas and observe all posted restrictions. Vehicles parked in fire lanes, emergency access routes or other prohibited areas may be towed.
 Stadium security and clear bag policy
 SC State's clear bag policy will be enforced at Oliver C. Dawson Stadium. Fans should review the policy before arriving and avoid bringing prohibited bags or items to stadium entrances.
 All spectators should be prepared for security screening. The university encourages attendees to travel light to help expedite entry.
 Weapons and other prohibited items are not permitted in the stadium. Fans should follow instructions from security personnel and report suspicious activity or safety concerns to the nearest law enforcement officer.
 Student and employee access
 Current SC State students must present valid university identification cards for campus and stadium access. SC State employees must have valid game tickets for stadium access. Employees should also carry their university identification cards and follow directions from security personnel at designated entry points.
 Access to certain parking areas, roads and facilities may be restricted during the event. University officials ask members of the campus community to allow additional travel time and cooperate with security personnel.
 Safety reminders
 SC State encourages everyone attending Saturday's game to remain aware of their surroundings, use designated pedestrian routes and follow instructions from law enforcement officers and event staff.
 Attendees should monitor official university communications for any changes to traffic patterns, parking arrangements or campus access procedures.
 The university appreciates the cooperation of the Bulldog community and visiting fans as SC State closes its regular-season schedule.
 Defending the HBCU National Championship
 Having won the MEAC championship, the Bulldogs will return to the Cricket Celebration Bowl at Mercedes-Benz Stadium in Atlanta, Georgia, on Saturday, Dec. 12, to defend their HBCU national title.
